questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country, the city, and the spoken language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy since most staff only speak in Turkish. The Erasmus Coordinator was very helpful, though, and explained me well and provided me with information in English.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance on course selection, learning materials, and signing up for student card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy, I searched beforehand and was lucky to find a place I could afford.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They need to look for a place some months or more before arrival, and they need to know that they will travel far with public transportation to get to the campus site.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's hard to say since I did not live there, so my ranking is based on what other students have told me

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a Turkish-speaking person (a friend of mine) with me to assist me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
To enter the campus and drive with the bus, you first need to register at the campus entrance and show your letter of acceptance to continue.
On arrival to the campus site, you register at the office of international students, then you are told to go and register at the Erasmus+ Office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Staff telling you in English where to go to register.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful after being correctly informed by the Erasmus+ Coordinator from host insititution.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive one week before the classes begin so you have enough time to register.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of my Turkish language course was B1
The level of my course in Avrupa'da Türkçe was C2, so I was following classes as good as I could.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was similar, maybe a bit less formal at the host organisation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
TÖMER (Turkish Language Course, B1)
Avrupa'da Türkçe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: TÖMER (Turkish Language Course) because it really helps you improve your language skills by challenging you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a bit more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with the cafés and cafeteria on campus, but I did not make use of the clubs, sport places, or anything else.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different types (theater plays, sport matches, sport day, running sessions, intercultural events), but most of them for Turkish-speaking students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intercultural event (Friendship Day) which was a good day to engage with other students and teachers at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city of Ankara, its many opportunities, and don't stay at the campus site only.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hard in the beginning, but it became easier during my stay.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a local organisation and become a volunteer together with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any specific, just the fact that everything is different and you need to create new daily routines. Maybe also the language barrier - the fact that so many Turkish citizens do not speak English makes it harder to adapt and feel that you belong.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality of the local people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-Grab the opportunity to learn the Turkish language by practicing as much as possible
-Get inspiration from other students, you might learn that their ways of doing things are also good
-Don't feel stupid or silly when you ask a lot of questions. Just ask as much as needed to get the information you need.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of something...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Practicing Turkish language to a high degree

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Connecting to my class mates and following the same fully-packed schedule every week.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
